crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: AI and Authorship
children.blurb: AI and authorship covers the questions of who, or what, can be credited as an author when artificial intelligence systems help produce text, images, code, music, or research outputs.

children.name: Fabricated Citations and Fact Checking
children.blurb: Fabricated citations and fact checking concerns the detection and prevention of references that do not exist, misattribute sources, or misrepresent what a source says.

children.name: Training Data and Academic Work
children.blurb: Training data and academic work covers the use of scholarly texts, including journal articles, preprints, theses, and course materials, as inputs for machine learning systems.

children.name: Ethics Review with AI Assistance
children.blurb: Ethics review with AI assistance covers the use of machine learning and natural language tools to support institutional review boards, research ethics committees, and journal editors in screening protocols, identifying risks, checking consent language, and flagging conflicts or missing safeguards.

children.name: Provenance of Research Images and Data
children.blurb: Provenance of research images and data is the record of where a dataset or image came from, how it was created or collected, who modified it, and under what conditions it can be reused.

sections.body: This field examines how AI changes the conduct and oversight of research. It covers who or what counts as an author, how fabricated citations are detected, where training data comes from, how ethics review can use AI assistance, and how images and data retain provenance. In practice, AI tools draft text, suggest references, summarize literature, screen protocols, and flag image duplication. Researchers and publishers use these tools to speed up parts of peer review and integrity checking. The work is not abstract, and it is embedded in submission systems, preprint checks, and institutional review workflows.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Some tasks are partly solved. Citation checking against databases and retraction notices is routine in many workflows, and image forensics can catch some duplication and splicing. Authorship rules remain unsettled because AI systems cannot take responsibility, and disclosure policies vary by journal and institution. Hallucinated references still appear in submitted manuscripts, and automated detectors produce false positives. Training data provenance is often opaque, especially for large models, and consent, licensing, and attribution are hard to verify at scale. Ethics review with AI assistance raises questions about bias, accountability, and the limits of automated judgment, and the honest limit is that AI can assist documentation and pattern finding but cannot replace human responsibility or institutional judgment.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The page on AI and Authorship examines credit, accountability, and disclosure when generative tools contribute to a manuscript. Fabricated Citations and Fact Checking looks at reference errors, invented sources, and the verification methods that catch them. Training Data and Academic Work considers where models get their text and data, and what that means for attribution and permission. Ethics Review with AI Assistance covers how review boards and researchers might use automated tools in protocol assessment and oversight. Provenance of Research Images and Data addresses tracking, integrity, and manipulation detection for figures, datasets, and supplementary files. Together these pages form a practical map of integrity controls across the research lifecycle, and the site's library of 135 research papers offers a starting point for readers who want to follow the underlying literature.
